instructions: Rinse the rice and put it in a pot with 1 3/4 cups water and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Bring to a boil, turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
In a bowl, mix the yogurt, 1 teaspoon of the ginger-garlic paste, 1/4 teaspoon of the chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon of the garam masala, 1/4 teaspoon of the kasuri methi and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt.
Cut the paneer into 1 inch cubes and stir them into the marinade until coated. Set aside while you make the gravy.
Chop the onion and the tomatoes. Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until it is golden.
Add the tomatoes, the sugar and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes are soft and broken down.
Stir in 3/4 teaspoon of the chili powder and 3/4 teaspoon of the garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell them. Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Blend the mixture with 3/4 cup water until completely smooth. That should be about 2 cups.
Wipe out the pan. Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil over medium heat. Add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaf and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute, until it no longer smells raw.
Pour in the blended sauce and another 3/4 cup water. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the paneer with all its marinade and cook for 2 minutes a side, 6 to 8 minutes in all, until browned in spots.
Rub the remaining 1 teaspoon kasuri methi between your palms into the sauce. Take out the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaf.
Stir in the cream, then add the paneer. Simmer gently for 2 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cilantro.
Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: Lead is Swasthi's Recipes (4.98 from 335): a spiced yogurt marinade on the paneer, a gravy of browned onion and tomato blended smooth, then whole spices, ginger-garlic and kasuri methi, with cream at the end. The lead's cashews are left out and the cream raised from 3 tablespoons to 6, as the page itself suggests for a nut-free version. The optional marinated onion and bell pepper are left out, and the paneer is browned in a skillet instead of grilled. It needs a blender. Naturally vegetarian and gluten-free; rice is the serving side because naan has wheat.
